restaurantLevelAllergenEvidence.summary: Individual foods may contact one another during preparation. Chipotle does not use egg, mustard, peanut, tree nut, sesame, shellfish, or fish as ingredients in its regular food but cannot guarantee their complete absence. This general statement is retained at restaurant level and is not smeared onto every item.

Corn tortillas, chips, and corn salsa may have trace gluten from possible co-mingling with gluten-containing grains in the field. This narrowly supports item-level may-contain gluten on the three named product types.

Limited-time or test products may contain allergens not identified on the regular allergen page. Chipotle Honey Chicken therefore remains allergen-unavailable rather than inheriting an empty allergen array.

adjudication.rationale: Research structure, current product mappings, direct allergen authority, target repair, Ingredient Intelligence timing, focused validation, and idempotency passed the POC terminal gates.

evidence.excerpt: Live restaurant-controlled U.S. web feed returned 26 named allergen-component rows. Positive codes were dair for milk, glut for the combined wheat/gluten category, soy, and sulp for the restaurant's disclosed vinegar-derived sulfites. Empty arrays were not treated as proof of allergen absence.

Official High Protein Menu presents six curated builds and Chicken or Steak High Protein Cups. These are size or composed presentations of the same enumerated ingredient products, not additional allergen-component identities.

Current official limited-time page says Chipotle Honey Chicken is available as a protein in burritos, bowls, salads, tacos, quesadillas, and a High Protein Cup, with availability varying by restaurant.
Official April 21, 2026 release states Chipotle Honey Chicken returned to restaurants across the United States beginning April 28 and can also be ordered in the High Protein Cup.
Official United States Chipotle homepage identifies the chain and currently promotes the nationwide return of Chipotle Honey Chicken for summer 2026.
Restaurant-controlled location ordering surface currently promotes Chipotle Honey Chicken and the High Protein Menu. It does not expose a separate linked-vendor allergen matrix.

Official U.S. Allergens & Special Diet page publishes the live allergen component, states wheat and gluten are combined because all gluten-containing Chipotle items contain wheat, identifies vinegar-derived sulfites below 10 ppm, warns that foods can contact one another, gives a specific trace-gluten warning for corn tortillas, chips, and corn salsa, and says limited-time or test items may include allergens not identified on the page.

Live restaurant-controlled U.S. ingredient feed provides ingredient membership for the regular menu components and corroborates milk in cheese and queso, soy in Sofritas, wheat in flour tortillas, and vinegar in the sulfite-coded products. Internal item IDs are presentation identifiers and are not globally one-to-one with the allergen feed.
